chunks: The Judge Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Salim ibn al-Bira' al-Hafiz al-Baghdadi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Razi narrated to me: My father narrated to me: My master Ali ibn Musa al-Rida narrated to me, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Hussein, from his father al-Hussein ibn Ali, from Ali (peace be upon them all).
He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Paradise longs for you, and for Ammar, and for Salman, and for Abu Dharr, and for Miqdad.
ai.seo_question: Who are the five individuals for whom Paradise longs according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Khisal*, this hadith utilizes a strong chain of transmission (isnad) linking directly to Imam Ali al-Rida, emphasizing the unique spiritual station of these five figures. It underscores the Shia concept of *wilayah* and the intrinsic connection between the faithful and the divine abode, positioning these individuals as beloved to Paradise itself. This narration serves as a theological affirmation of their purity and enduring legacy within the broader Islamic community.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-81 Al-Qazi Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Salim ibn al-Bira’ al-Hafiz al-Baghdady narrated that Al-Hassan ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Razi quoted his father, on the authority of his Master Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hussein as-Sajjad (MGB), on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB)
that the Prophet (MGB) told him, “Paradise is eager for you - Ali, Ammar, Salman, Abuzar and Miqdad.”
